text:
maria (PM): quick sync — I sketched a proposal for gating Dedicated autoscale features by customer commitment level. goal: give predictable headroom to paying customers while keeping operational cost bounded. asking for quick feedback + owners.

sam (SRE): +1 on gating. we need hard launch criteria: telemetry, SLOs, rollback plan. otherwise oncall will get paged by noisy scale events.

jess (EngProd): agree. propose these gating dimensions: 1) commit size (monthly GPU hours), 2) SLA tier, 3) burst-credit allowance, 4) telemetry completeness (latency, queue depth, preempt rate).

alex (Sales): from GTM, customers expect 'burst' in higher tiers. Sales wants a simple mapping we can include in contracts. Prefer: Bronze/Silver/Gold with clear numeric thresholds.

toni (CSE): we also need an onboarding checklist for customers to opt into autoscale: workload profile, warmup prompt sets, allowed model families. otherwise unexpected token-costs and quality regressions.

maria (PM): rough matrix I put in the doc:
```
Gold: annual commit >= 10k GPU-hours -> autoscale + burst + preempt-protection window
Silver: annual commit 2k-10k -> burst w/ soft preemption, limited sustained autoscale to 2x baseline
Bronze: <2k -> no autoscale, manual scaling only (self-service)
```
We need to pick exact numbers and whether we enforce by billing or by tenant config. thoughts?

sam (SRE): enforce via tenant config on control plane, but billing flags should unlock higher quotas. That lets infra check limits before serving. Also need these metrics before GA: 99th latency for hot path, preempt rate < 0.5% over 24h, autoscale churn < 10% of requests.

jess (EngProd): instrumentation to add: per-tenant burst-credit balance, peak GPU utilization windows, autoscale-trigger histogram, and a dry-run mode for 2 weeks (simulated autoscale without actually provisioning GPUs). dry-run will help customers validate.

alex (Sales): dry-run is a big sell — helps close deals. can we make dry-run part of Silver trials?

toni (CSE): yes but require a 1-week onboarding session. Also must document expected behavior when a customer hits a preempt: priority fallback to smaller model or queueing policy. Customers need an explicit SLA doc.

maria (PM): ops/questions for tradeoffs: 
- do we allow burst credit gifting between tenants in the same org?
- how do we price burst vs sustained autoscale?
- what are minimum headroom buffers we reserve for emergency fallbacks?

sam (SRE): do NOT allow gifting across orgs. within an org OK but needs accounting. minimum headroom: reserve 10% of pool capacity per region for emergency fallbacks for Gold. That number may change after load tests.

jess (EngProd): pricing: suggest burst priced as ephemeral GPU-hours at 1.5x base rate; sustained autoscale billable as normal usage but requires commit. Implementation note: need to add a policy engine in control plane to evaluate request against quota + commit + temp-burst balance.

alex (Sales): pricing sounds reasonable. we'll need a simple explainer table for contracts. can product produce a mock SLA/handout by EOD Friday?

maria (PM): action items:
- jess: prototype control-plane gating rules + dry-run flag (owner) — target PR by next Wed
- sam: define telemetry guardrails + test plan for headroom (owner) — target test plan by Tue
- toni: customer onboarding checklist draft + fallback playbook — target draft by Fri
- alex: narrative + contract language draft — collab with maria — target by Fri

ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-4321 to track control-plane policy work.

maria (PM): if no objections, I'll fold these into the dedicated roadmap doc and set a follow-up sync next Tuesday to finalize numeric thresholds. :thumbsup:

alex (Sales): :thumbsup: fine from GTM.

sam (SRE): noted. will add preliminary load thresholds to INFRA-4321.

jess (EngProd): I'll start the prototype and post a short demo in the channel when ready.

toni (CSE): will coordinate onboarding templates with docs.

maria (PM): thanks — closing the loop here.
